title: Deferred allocation leak causing tenant burst suppression during high-throughput windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a customer-facing traffic surge on 2026-03-01 we observed that several tenants with burst credits were unable to consume their burst allowance. Instead of scaling reserved pool slots to accommodate the load, the allocator reported saturated headroom while telemetry showed idle GPUs. Investigation found a deferred-allocation ledger leak: slot lease entries were left in a pending state after preemptive rebalance operations, causing the allocator to undercount free capacity (effectively suppressing tenant burst).

What happened (timeline):
- 2026-03-01 02:12 UTC: Traffic spike from three customers running bursty workloads. Latency and error rates rose for those tenants.
- 02:13 UTC: Internal alert (autoscaler:headroom < threshold) triggered and attempted scale-up of reserved pool but decision engine chose fallback policy instead of immediate allocation due to perceived zero headroom.
- 02:15 UTC: SREs started investigating; dashboard showed GPUs with low utilization in the affected hostpool.
- 02:20 UTC: We traced discrepancy to allocator ledger: a set of lease records remained in DEFERRED_PENDING state because the lease-renewal path did not clear entries when leader preempted the slot.
- 02:34 UTC: Emergency mitigation (hotfix v1) deployed to prize stale deferred entries and allow reallocation.
- 03:10 UTC: Services recovered to normal; customers notified and incident comms sent.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis validated by reproducer):
- A timing window exists when the rebalancer runs concurrent with leader preemption and the deferred allocation path returns before the lease removal callback completes. In that window a lease is moved to an indeterminate state (DEFERRED_PENDING) but the headroom accounting counter is not decremented, leaving the global "available slots" metric artificially low.
- The autoscaler has logic that short-circuits immediate allocations when headroom is reported as zero; this combined with the ledger leak prevented fastest-path allocations during bursts.
- The issue is most likely to surface for: high cardinality tenants, short-lived burst traffic, and environments with frequent leader-flapping (edge AP/region migrations).

Immediate mitigations performed: 
- Hotfix v1 (rollback-safe): prize-stale-deferred-entries job that runs a best-effort scan and clears stuck pending leases if their last-update timestamp is > 30s. Rolled to canary (10% traffic) at 02:28 UTC, full rollout by 02:34 UTC. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/4782
- Emergency configuration change: reduce the autoscaler short-circuit threshold for headroom from 0 -> -2 (allow two speculative allocations) while we stabilize metrics. Config change link: https://go/redwood/configs/autoscaler#speculative-allocation
- Customer comms: Support issued targeted messages to impacted tenants and opened follow-ups for affected accounts (ACME Health, Shoply).

Permanent fixes planned / in progress: 
1) Ledger invariants + stronger GC: ensure every deferred allocation path has an idempotent removal callback; add late-reconciliation that replays leader-election outcomes to the ledger. "ENG-119001-1" tracked here as a subtask.
2) Allocator accounting test harness: a deterministic simulator that reproduces the leader-preempt/rebalance ordering to catch this class of races in CI.
3) Autoscaler safety changes: introduce a short speculative allocation window (configurable) plus an alert when speculative allocations exceed X% of pool.
4) Telemetry improvements: emit per-tenant ledger depth, deferred-count, and a headroom_consistency_check gauge to detect ledger vs. cluster-state drift.
5) Add a canary gating rule to Block scale-down for 5m after a large speculative scale-up to avoid flip-flop.

Current status (as of 2026-03-14):
- Hotfix v1 is live and has prevented recurrence for two subsequent bursts.
- Engineering has a passing unit + integration test that reproduces the leak locally.
- PR for the invariant + cleanup (https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/4821) is in review; planned rollout to canary on 2026-03-16.

Risk/Trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive GC risks killing legitimate in-flight allocations; the hotfix uses a conservative 30s threshold and logs for manual review.
- Speculative allocations increase burst capacity but may temporarily oversubscribe GPUs if multiple speculative allocations succeed; mitigated via a low default (-2) and per-tenant limits.

Rollout plan for permanent fix: 
- Merge PRs after security and performance review.
- Canary rollout in controlled region (eu-central-1) for 24h with canary dashboards.
- If stable, progressive expansion to all Dedicated regions over 48h.
- Post-rollout: run headroom_consistency_check for 72h and close ticket after 7 days of no regression.

Owner notes and comms: 
- Engineering lead: Leo Chen (assignee).
- SRE contact: Maria Gomez.
- PM point: David Rosen.
- Notified customers: ACME Health, Shoply, ZenithRetail.

Link to incident timeline and dashboard: https://go/redwood/incidents/2026-03-01-deferred-alloc-leak
